reason: Every measurement in the finding reproduces, and it is past what either gate proves. Driven at 390x844 with hasTouch+isMobile (matchMedia confirms pointer:coarse true, hover:none true, hover:hover false, pointer:fine false) against ?v=light&state=full: at rest .dot[0] computes --disc #71717a with ::before box-shadow rgb(113,113,122) inset; after one touchscreen.tap el.matches(':hover') is true, --disc is #111111 and the ring is rgb(17,17,17); after the second tap tip.classList.contains('on') is false and the mark is still #111111 with :hover still true; after window.scrollBy(0,300) it is still #111111. I pushed past the finding: a REAL touch swipe-scroll (CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent touchStart/8x touchMove/touchEnd at x=300, well clear of the strip) does NOT release it either, and scrolling the mark fully off-screen and back returns it still inked. So the residue survives the two gestures a reader actually performs after dismissing a tip. interaction-check.mjs:461-487 drives exactly this tap/second-tap/tap-away sequence but only ever asserts on #tip's class list; it never reads the mark's own --disc, so nothing here restates a proven assertion. Not a re-file: stale-tip-strands-on-scroll (r1) is the label stranding, mark-hit-theft-at-390 (r1) is the hit box, rise-fill-outranks-every-interaction-rule (r2) is animation-origin rank on .rise; none of them touch this cascade. Two of the seat's consequence sentences are overstated and I am correcting them rather than refuting on them. (1) 'every tap leaves another false emphasis behind' is false as measured - hover MOVES, it does not accumulate: tapping .dot[4] returned .dot[0] to #71717a and inked only [4], and a tap on empty ground cleared it entirely. Exactly one mark is ever wrong at a time. (2) 'the most emphatic mark in the strip' is overstated - the three past-fortnight marks are a SOLID 12px #4f46e5 disc and a 2px #111111 hollow stroke does not out-weigh them by area. The real and sufficient harm is narrower: within the hollow-ring class, which is its actual peer group, one arbitrary young mark stands at 18.9:1 against paper while its five peers stand at 4.25:1, carrying the surface's strongest ink with no state behind it - not pinned, not focused, not past the fortnight - and it stays that way until the reader happens to touch something else. On a lock whose whole rule is that status is ink density and fill, that is a real defect and it is the width where reading is most touch-driven. Severity 'defect' is correct: visibly wrong but passable, and no untruth is asserted, because a hollow black ring is not one of the two states in the language so the reader cannot decode it as 'past the fortnight'. The proposed fix is sound in shape and its numbers are right against the real source: .dot.old (0-2-0, line 396) then .dot.pinned (0-2-0) then .dot:active (0-2-0, line 399) resolves by source order exactly as the seat says, pinned beats old, press beats pinned; show(el, pin) and drop() are the right two hooks because drop() is already the single retirement path for a touch pin (the pointerdown handler at 1187, the capture-phase tap-away, Escape, and onMove when the mark scrolls out), so the class can never outlive the pin; and it adds no colour, no weight and no object, so it is actionable on a frozen surface. It is not wrong, it is incomplete - see sharpenedFix.
sharpenedFix: Take the seat's three CSS rules and two script lines verbatim, then close the instance it missed. The same latch is on the tab strip and it is the more consequential one: .tab:hover { color: var(--ink); } at lately.html:196, on anchors that are href="#" and navigate nowhere. Measured at 390 with touch: at rest the two inactive tabs are rgb(113,113,122)/400 and Lately is rgb(17,17,17)/600; after one tap on 'Today's Signal' it is rgb(17,17,17)/400 and stays there through a 600px scroll. Two tabs then read at full ink and only weight 600 and the 2px ::after underline still separate the current one, so the tap degrades the surface's navigation signal, not just a chart mark. Move that rule into the same gate: replace .tab:hover { color: var(--ink); } with @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) { .tab:hover { color: var(--ink); } }, keeping it before .tab[aria-current="page"] so the current tab's ink and weight are untouched. Leave .btn:hover (line 470) alone - a latched paper-3 background on the error state's one control is benign and is the only press feedback a coarse pointer gets there. One correction to the seat's wording: declare the pinned rule as .dot.pinned, not alongside :focus-visible in the same selector list, or a pinned mark inherits the focus outline it never earned.
breaks: Hybrid devices are the known cost: a touch laptop or an iPad with a trackpad reports (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) because the media query describes the PRIMARY pointer, so the sticky hover returns there for finger input. That is the standard trade-off for this remedy and it is strictly better than the current state, but it means the fix is a mitigation on hybrids, not a cure. Re-measure after it lands: (1) interaction-check.mjs:1330 is a styleSheets selector-text grep for '.dot:active' - it still passes because that rule is untouched, but note the same block's own comment already concedes it is 'a cheap declaration check', and nesting .dot:hover inside a media query means any future selector-text assertion that greps '.dot:hover' would need to walk CSSMediaRule.cssRules or it will silently start passing on a rule it can no longer see - the exact vacuous-assertion failure mode round 2 was written to kill. (2) interaction-check.mjs:445-456 hovers .dot.old with a real mouse in a desktop context; confirm the media query still matches there so 'a real pointer over a mark names it' and the ink change both survive. (3) Add the assertion this finding exposes, since none exists: after tap, tap-again, and a touch swipe-scroll at 390, assert every .dot computes --disc equal to its rest value, and assert no .tab that is not [aria-current] computes color #111111. (4) audit.mjs needs no new pair - .dot.pinned ring #111111 on paper is the same composite the hover state already declared - but re-run it to confirm the coarse-pointer rest state of the marks (#71717a ring, 4.25:1) is what the non-text floor check now sees on the phone viewport, since the hover ink used to be the value present after the gate's own taps.
